senses.definition: A long tool strung with hair or another fiber, drawn across strings to play a violin or a related instrument.
senses.example: The violinist drew the bow across the lowest string.

senses.definition: A container, often with straight sides and a lid, for holding things.
senses.example: I found a box of crayons on the shelf.

senses.definition: An outlined space where you can write an answer, press a button, or mark a choice.
senses.example: Put a check in the box beside your choice.

senses.definition: To put something into a box.
senses.example: We boxed the books before moving them.

senses.definition: To take part in a sport where people wearing gloves try to hit each other within agreed rules.
senses.example: She learned to box at a sports club.

senses.definition: An organized refusal to buy, use, or take part in something in order to protest.
senses.example: The boycott lasted more than a year as residents refused to ride the buses.

senses.definition: A band, chain, or other piece of jewelry worn around the wrist.
senses.example: My bracelet has three blue beads.

senses.definition: A mark used in a pair around words, numbers, or other marks.
senses.example: Put a square bracket on each side of the missing note.

senses.definition: A piece that holds up or joins parts of something.
senses.example: A metal bracket held the shelf against the wall.

senses.definition: A little salty, as water can be where a river mixes with the sea.
senses.example: The marsh creek held brackish water when the tide came in.

senses.definition: To talk with a lot of pride about what you have done or what you own.
senses.example: I was proud of my win, but I tried not to brag.

senses.definition: A length of hair, thread, or another material woven from several strands.
senses.example: One braid slipped loose while I ran.

senses.definition: To make this pattern by weaving strands over one another.
senses.example: We braided three long pieces of yarn.

senses.definition: A way to read and write using patterns of raised dots that can be felt with the fingers.
senses.example: A sign with braille let the visitor check the room number by touch.

senses.definition: The organ inside your head that takes in signals and helps control the body.
senses.example: Your brain helps you remember what you learned yesterday.

senses.definition: The outer layers of a grain that may be taken off when it is milled.
senses.example: Brown rice still has bran around its lighter center.

senses.definition: A part of a tree or bush that grows out from the trunk or another stem.
senses.example: A robin landed on the lowest branch.

senses.definition: One part of a larger group or system.
senses.example: There is a branch of our library near the park.

senses.definition: To split and go in more than one direction.
senses.example: The walking paths branch at the big rock.

senses.definition: A name or mark used to identify a company’s products.
senses.example: Both backpacks came from the same brand.

senses.definition: An instrument played by buzzing into a mouthpiece, such as a trumpet or trombone.
senses.example: A trumpet player makes a brass instrument sound by buzzing their lips.

senses.definition: Ready to do something even when you are afraid or it is difficult.
senses.example: It felt brave to speak up when a classmate needed help.

senses.definition: To face something unpleasant or hard.
senses.example: We braved the wind to finish the walk.

senses.definition: A food usually made from flour and water, shaped and cooked.
senses.example: We cut the bread into thick slices.

senses.definition: To split something into pieces or stop it from working properly.
senses.example: The toy could break if it falls onto the stone floor.

senses.definition: To fail to follow a rule or keep a promise.
senses.example: I would rather lose a turn than break the rules.

senses.definition: A short pause in an activity.
senses.example: We took a ten-minute break from the lesson.

senses.definition: To separate a difficult idea or job into smaller parts that are easier to understand or do.
senses.example: Dad helped me break the report down into three short sections.

senses.definition: To help people feel more comfortable and start talking when they first meet or feel shy.
senses.example: The teacher asked everyone to share a favorite snack to break the ice.

senses.definition: The first meal of the day.
senses.example: I had eggs and toast for breakfast.

senses.definition: The air that moves into or out of your lungs when you breathe, or one time you take that air in or let it out.
senses.example: I took a deep breath before I started reading aloud.

senses.definition: To take air or another gas in and let it out again, as people do with their lungs.
senses.example: I stopped running for a moment so I could breathe more easily.

senses.definition: A light wind.
senses.example: A cool breeze moved the curtains.

senses.definition: Something that is very easy to do.
senses.example: After some practice, the warm-up puzzle was a breeze.

senses.definition: A hard, usually rectangular block used to build things.
senses.example: One red brick was missing from the garden wall.

senses.definition: A structure that gives people or vehicles a way across water, a road, or another gap.
senses.example: We crossed the river on a wooden bridge.

senses.definition: To connect two sides of a gap or join things that seem far apart.
senses.example: The path and stepping stones bridge the gap between the lawns.

senses.definition: Lasting a short time or using few words.
senses.example: There was a brief pause before we heard the answer.

senses.definition: To give someone the facts or instructions they need for a job.
senses.example: Our guide will brief us on the trail rules.

senses.definition: Giving a lot of light or easy to see because of strong color.
senses.example: The bright lamp lets me read at night.

senses.definition: Quick to learn and understand.
senses.example: The bright student found two ways to solve the problem.

senses.definition: Shining very brightly, or having a strong and bright color.
senses.example: A brilliant green light shone through the glass.

senses.definition: Exceptionally good or clever.
senses.example: That was a brilliant way to fit all the pieces in the box.

senses.definition: To carry or guide someone or something to a place or to another person.
senses.example: Please bring your library book to school tomorrow.

senses.definition: Quick and full of energy, or cool in a way that makes you feel awake.
senses.example: We took a brisk walk before lunch.

senses.definition: Wide from side to side, or covering many subjects.
senses.example: We followed a broad path through the woods.

senses.definition: A vegetable with a thick green stem that divides into small groups of flower buds.
senses.example: We added broccoli to the soup.

senses.definition: A tool with stiff fibers on a long handle, used to sweep floors or other surfaces.
senses.example: I used a broom to clear leaves off the steps.

senses.definition: A boy or man who has one or more parents in common with you, including through adoption.
senses.example: My brother taught me a new card game.

senses.definition: An app that requests and shows web pages.
senses.example: I opened a library website in my browser.

senses.definition: An area that changes color after tissues under the surface are hurt, often without a cut.
senses.example: A purple bruise appeared on my knee after I bumped the chair.

senses.definition: To cause an injury like this, or to damage soft fruit by pressing on it.
senses.example: Dropping the bag can bruise the peaches.

senses.definition: A tool with hair, wire, or other stiff strands, used to clean, paint, or make something smooth.
senses.example: Rinse your paint brush after class.

senses.definition: To use a brush on something, or to touch it lightly while passing by.
senses.example: The tall grass brushed my knees.

senses.definition: A small space filled with gas in a liquid, or a thin film with gas inside.
senses.example: A bubble rose to the top of my glass.

senses.definition: To form bubbles or rise in bubbles.
senses.example: The soup started to bubble.

senses.definition: An open container, usually with a handle, used for carrying things such as water or sand.
senses.example: We filled a bucket with water for the plants.

senses.definition: A friend or a person paired with you for an activity.
senses.example: My reading buddy helped me find the next page.

senses.definition: An error in software or computer equipment that makes it work differently from how it should.
senses.example: A bug made the game jump back to the start.

senses.definition: To make something by putting parts or materials together.
senses.example: We used blocks to build a tunnel.

senses.definition: A short plant stem with thick layers that store food, often found underground.
senses.example: A tulip bulb can grow a fresh shoot in spring.

senses.definition: A raised part on a surface, or a small hit or jolt.
senses.example: The cart jumped when it rolled over a bump.

senses.definition: To hit or come against something, often by accident.
senses.example: Watch your head so you do not bump the low shelf.

senses.definition: A group of things held together or gathered in one spot.
senses.example: I found a bunch of keys by the door.

senses.definition: To gather closely or push things together.
senses.example: The runners bunched up near the finish.

senses.definition: A group of things tied, wrapped, or held together.
senses.example: We carried a bundle of sticks to the shed.

senses.definition: To gather and wrap things together.
senses.example: I bundled the old papers with string.

senses.definition: The upward push that a liquid or gas gives to something in it.
senses.example: The buoyancy of the water helped hold the boat up.

senses.definition: To be on fire, give off heat, or be damaged by fire or heat.
senses.example: The toast began to burn in the toaster.

senses.definition: A place on a body or object harmed by heat or something similar.
senses.example: The cook used a thick oven mitt to avoid a burn.

senses.definition: An underground passage or home made or used by an animal.
senses.example: The meerkat ran into its burrow when another meerkat called.

senses.definition: To break open suddenly, or to start doing something suddenly and strongly.
senses.example: The balloon burst when it hit a sharp branch.

senses.definition: A sudden, short period of sound, movement, or energy.
senses.example: We heard a burst of laughter from the next room.

senses.definition: To put something under earth, sand, or other material and cover it.
senses.example: The squirrel buried an acorn beside the path.

senses.definition: Having a lot to do, being used, or full of activity.
senses.example: The path was busy with people heading to school.

senses.definition: To keep yourself or someone else occupied.
senses.example: I busied myself with a puzzle while I waited.

senses.definition: An insect with broad wings, often brightly colored, that grows from a caterpillar.
senses.example: A black-and-orange butterfly rested on the fence.

senses.definition: A small piece used to fasten clothing.
senses.example: I found a missing button in my coat pocket.

senses.definition: A control that you push, click, or tap to make something happen.
senses.example: Press the green button to start the game.

senses.definition: To fasten clothing with buttons.
senses.example: I buttoned my coat before going outside.

senses.definition: To get something by paying money for it.
senses.example: We saved enough to buy a new soccer ball.

senses.definition: The release of pollen when a bee shakes a flower with its muscles.
senses.example: Buzz pollination shook pollen free from the tomato flower.

senses.definition: A group of eight bits that a computer handles as a unit.
senses.example: A file with 100 bytes contains 800 bits.
